title: Unraveling the Helix Nebula: Its Structure and Knots

evidence.locator: Sect. III.1: the main ring is an inner ring, an ellipse of 499 x 459 arcsec, and an outer ring, an ellipse of 742 x 446 arcsec: circles of radius 250 and 371 arcsec seen at tilt angles of 23 and 53 degrees out of the plane of the sky. Sect. III and Fig. 15: the inner ring expands with a maximum radial component of 15.5 km/s and the outer ring 25.5 km/s, spatial expansion 40 and 32 km/s, ages 6,560 and 12,100 yr; the nebula expands homologously. Sect. IV: the more distant side of the inner disc's axis is at position angle 288 degrees by the ring's orientation and radial-velocity pattern, 303 degrees by its plumes; the outer ring's at about 168 degrees; the outer features share the outer ring's orientation; the inner disc is a 'hockey puck' with lower-density gas above it; the outermost ring is 1,500 arcsec across.
